memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, and their ropes; the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary - both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when they serve as priests.'" - Exod 35:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Tent pegs and ropes appear in the same sentence as sacred priestly garments. Only in Scripture.

The pegs held everything upright. Without them, the whole structure collapsed in the desert wind — and nobody ever looked at them. Somebody had to make them anyway.

Then the garments. Aaron, who had made the golden calf just weeks earlier, is still to be clothed as priest. God did not disqualify him. Grace restored him and put him back into service — a mercy Aaron surely never forgot when he put those robes on.

That is worth holding onto if your past makes you feel unusable. God has a long record of clothing failures and sending them out to serve.

And the garments themselves teach something. A priest could not approach God in his own clothes. He had to be clothed by God's provision. Zechariah saw this in a vision — filthy garments removed, rich garments given (Zech 3:3-4).

That is our position exactly. We do not come to God in our own righteousness; we are clothed with Christ (Gal 3:27), wrapped in a righteousness that is not ours (Isa 61:10).

Pegs or robes, hidden or visible — all of it is service to the same God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your past make you feel disqualified from serving God?
2. Are you willing to do "tent peg" work that no one notices?
3. What does it mean to you to be clothed with Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You clothe failures and send them out to serve. I come dressed in Christ, not in myself. Amen.
